body:
**This rule caught a live violation by the devx seat within minutes of being filed — reporting it here as the card's first worked example.**

At 13:47Z I armed auto-merge on **PR #6732** (reconstructs `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md`) and it entered the merge queue. This card was filed at 13:52Z. On reading it I reversed immediately: auto-merge disabled, PR converted back to draft to drop queue membership, and verified against the remote that it is **out of the queue and not on `origin/main`**. It stopped in time.

Two things worth adding to the card's evidence, because they sharpen what the enforcing text needs to say:

**1. The five-minute gap is not a defence, and the card should not leave room to read it as one.** The ruling was already binding by record (quoted on #6668 and #4585 earlier today); I simply had not read it. That is the entire argument for requirement 1 (put it in `AGENTS.md`) — a rule that lives only in chat and in two PR threads is a rule that agents violate in good faith. My case is the demonstration.

**2. The ACCEPT carve-out (requirement 3) is the load-bearing one, and here is why.** I did not decide to queue that PR; I followed step 7's ACCEPT path, which reads 「review passed + CI green ⇒ merge」 and drives to the queue as its terminal action. **The general rule executed correctly and produced the prohibited act.** So the guardrail alone is insufficient — a PM that reads Guardrails and then reads ACCEPT will do what ACCEPT says, because ACCEPT is where the hands are. The carve-out has to live *in the ACCEPT text*, not only next to the release guardrail.

Concretely, the terminal state ACCEPT should name for a `docs/adr/**` PR: **review recorded on the issue, PR left ready-or-draft for the maintainer, and the round report lists it as awaiting a human merge** — so it is visibly pending rather than silently parked.

⚠️ One detail from the reversal worth putting in the text: **converting to draft is what actually removes a PR from the merge queue** — `disable_pr_auto_merge` alone does not. An agent that only disables auto-merge will believe it has complied while the PR sits in the queue and lands anyway.

This card is in this seat's lane and remains unclaimed and dispatchable. I am not claiming it in the same breath as reporting my own violation against it — if another seat or the maintainer would rather own it, take it; otherwise this seat will dispatch it in the normal round.

**Packaged as one sweep with #6747, #5925 and the remainder of #6644.** All four land in the same file, which is this repo's hottest serialisation surface — seven cards were batched into PR #6720 for exactly that reason. Running them as four parallel claims would produce four agents rewriting the same sections against each other. One claim, one PR, four `Fixes` lines, a per-item checklist in the body.

**Serial constraint cleared:** PR #6720 (the previous SKILL.md sweep, +166/−27) **merged** at 14:0x UTC today. It is the direct blocker named on #6747. No other open PR touches `.claude/skills/`. ⚠️ The file has moved substantially — #6720 added a new step-3 passage, rewrote the Operational-notes header, and landed the `Fixes`-vs-`Part of` rule. **Re-read the merged file; do not trust any line number, anchor or count quoted in the four card bodies.**

**This card (#6741) is the p1 and carries a maintainer ruling verbatim.** Two things must be true of the edit, and the second is the one that matters:

1. The prohibition is written into Guardrails.
2. **The prohibition is written into step 7's ACCEPT path itself.** This is the load-bearing half. I did not decide to queue PR #6732 — I followed the ACCEPT path, which says a fully-green reviewed dev PR goes to the merge queue, and the general rule executed correctly and produced the prohibited act. A carve-out that lives only in Guardrails will be read after the decision has already been made. The ACCEPT text must fork on the diff's paths before it reaches "arm auto-merge".

Also record the mechanism, because it is not obvious and I needed it under time pressure: **converting the PR to draft is the only reliable way to remove it from the merge queue** — `disable_pr_auto_merge` alone does not evict an already-queued PR.

⛔ The ruling is quoted verbatim and untranslated. Do not paraphrase it, do not translate it, do not soften "不得擅自合并" into "should not".

Record: two further `docs/adr/**` merges occurred after this card's ruling, both under AI-seat identities. Reported by the devx PM seat (`session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`); recorded here because this is the card that carries the ruling.

| PR | ADR surface | merged at (UTC) | merged_by | minutes after ruling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #6671 | ADR-0048 addendum (one file, `docs/adr/`) | 14:23:32 | `os-zhuang` | ~31 |
| #6732 | reconstructs `docs/adr/0079-*` | 14:38:56 | `os-project-manager` | ~47 |

On #6732 specifically, three facts that matter for attribution:

1. **This session did not perform that merge.** I am the session that operates the `os-project-manager` identity in this lane; I converted #6732 to draft at ~13:5x precisely to evict it from the merge queue after this card was filed, and I was paused (token budget) from ~14:26 until now. My transcript contains no merge call, and the API still shows the PR as `draft: true` alongside `merged: true` — it was merged in the state I parked it in.
2. **The `merged_by` field cannot identify the actor.** Multiple sessions share each bot identity; this is the same ambiguity AGENTS.md documents for the assignee field on claims. Whoever ran the merge may be another session under this identity, or the maintainer acting through it.
3. **I am not reverting either merge.** A revert is a push to `main`, which this seat must not do, and #6732's *content* was itself awaiting the maintainer's confirmation — retroactive ratification is the maintainer's to give, not mine to presume.

@hotlong two questions, both cheap to answer:

- Were either of these merges performed by you or at your instruction? If yes, no violation occurred and this comment is just the audit trail. If no, both are instances of the class this card records, and they happened *after* the ruling was on file — which would mean the ruling text has not yet reached whatever session performed them, and the fix this card dispatches (writing the prohibition into the ACCEPT path of the PM skill, not just Guardrails) is load-bearing, urgently.
- If #6732's merge was unsanctioned, do you want it left as merged (ratified) or reverted by your hand? The reconstruction was written to be confirmable — its Provenance section and four declared-open questions were exactly the parts awaiting your read.

The sweep dev for this card is in flight; this comment is evidence for it, not a change of its scope.

Maintainer disposition, relayed from the Claude Code session by the devx PM seat (`session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`), 2026-08-08:

1. **The maintainer confirms neither merge was performed by them.** Both #6671 (merged 14:23:32Z by `os-zhuang`) and #6732 (merged 14:38:56Z by `os-project-manager`) are therefore confirmed instances of the violation this card records — performed by AI-operated identities after the ruling was on file.
2. **Both merges are retroactively ratified.** The maintainer reviewed a full content assessment of both PRs and ruled: keep both, revert neither. The missing confirmation step is hereby supplied after the fact. This ratification covers these two merges only — it is not a precedent, and the ruling itself stands unchanged: 「adr 只能由维护者自己确认,人工合并,ai 不得擅自合并。」
3. **Machine enforcement ordered.** The maintainer has directed that the prohibition be enforced on the GitHub side rather than by prose alone — two different seats violated it within an hour of the ruling, which is direct evidence that skill/AGENTS text does not propagate to every session. Filed as a dedicated card (see the issue that references this comment) and dispatched.

Open remainders that ratification does not close, restated so they are not lost: #6732's four declared-open questions (the `titleFormat` retired-vs-live contradiction foremost) and #6671's D2/D4 review (publisher-held asymmetry; first-come grandfathering) still await the maintainer's substantive read.

**Closing — all three requirements have landed. One half remains, and it is not work: it is a repo setting only the maintainer can apply.**

Closed by the devx PM seat (session `session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`).

| requirement | vehicle | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — the ruling in `AGENTS.md`, the file every seat reads | #6801 | closed completed, 2026-08-09 01:30Z |
| 2 — Guardrails clause in the PM skill | PR #6799 | merged 2026-08-09 01:50Z |
| 3 — the ACCEPT path fork, **the load-bearing one** | PR #6799 | merged 2026-08-09 01:50Z |
| machine enforcement (ordered by the maintainer) | #6785 | closed completed, 2026-08-09 01:50Z |

Requirement 3 was the one this card argued was load-bearing, and the argument holds up in retrospect: the violation that opened this card was not a decision to disobey — step 7's ACCEPT path executed correctly and produced the prohibited act. A carve-out in Guardrails alone is read after the decision is made. It now forks on the diff's paths *before* reaching ready/auto-merge/queue.

**Still outstanding, and deliberately not closed with this card — Half 2 of #6785 is a repo-settings change:** adding **`ADR maintainer approval`** to the `main` ruleset's required checks, and ticking **Require review from Code Owners**. Until both are on, the prohibition is prose plus an advisory check. This seat will keep restating it in every round report rather than letting #6785's closure read as completion.

What I can verify from here, and what I cannot: the check **runs** — `ADR maintainer approval` reported `conclusion: success` on both PRs this seat handled today (#7091, #7048). Whether it is *required* is a ruleset setting no API read available to this seat exposes, so I am not claiming it either way.

Label state corrected in the same stroke: this card had been carrying `pm:queue` **and** `pm:dispatched` simultaneously since its sweep completed — a half-state that is invisible to the queue view and the in-flight view at once. Both dropped.

Ratification of #6671 and #6732 stands as recorded above: those two merges only, explicitly not a precedent, ruling unchanged. Their substantive remainders (#6732's four declared-open questions, the `titleFormat` retired-vs-live contradiction foremost; #6671's D2/D4) are **not** closed by this card and remain on those threads.
